AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To evaluate the effects of levothyroxine (L-T4) supplementation on growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 3 years of age in very low birth weight (VLBW) infants with transient hypothyroxinemia of prematurity (THOP).

AbstractText.Label: STUDY DESIGN
AbstractText.content: VLBW infants with plasma thyroid-stimulating hormone concentrations <10 mIU l-1 and free thyroxine concentrations <0.8 ng dl-1 were defined as having THOP and randomly assigned to the Treated (20 infants) or Untreated (31 infants) group. The Treated group received L-T4 at a dose of 5 μg kg-1 day-1. Growth and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 3 years of age were compared between the two groups.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: There were no significant differences in body length, body weight or head circumference mean s.d. scores or in neurodevelopmental outcomes between the two groups.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: L-T4 supplementation in VLBW infants with THOP demonstrated no beneficial effect at 3 years of age.
